c.tagline: Siberia's wooden-laced 'Paris', gateway to Lake Baikal and the Decembrists' exile.

taxi.fareNote: Book through the Yandex Go app rather than hailing on the street, where unmetered cabs overcharge. Foreign-issued Visa/Mastercard no longer work in Russia, so set the app to cash or pay the driver in rubles.

emergency.note: 112 is the universal emergency number reachable from any phone, including without SIM or credit.

avoid.reason: Late-night drunken altercations near bars and petty theft in crowded markets and marshrutkas warrant normal vigilance.

hood_desc: The administrative and walkable heart of Irkutsk around Kirov Square, the Angara River embankment and the Church of the Saviour; best for first-timers who want everything within reach.
A restored quarter of gingerbread wooden houses turned into restaurants, bars, craft shops and a mall - Irkutsk's liveliest dining and nightlife zone, buzzing in the evenings.
The historic streets around the Volkonsky and Trubetskoy house-museums, where exiled Decembrists settled after 1825; atmospheric wooden mansions and quiet lanes for history lovers.
Irkutsk's main shopping spine - pedestrian Uritskogo Street and Karl Marx Street lined with boutiques, department stores and cafes, with the Central Market nearby.
A leafy academic district on the left bank near Irkutsk State University's campuses and research institutes; calm, green and residential, popular with students and families.
lodging: Courtyard by Marriott Irkutsk City Center
Silk Road - Shelkovniy Put Boutique Hotel

water.note: Locals often boil tap water; bottled or boiled is the safer choice.

transit.pay: Fares are paid in cash to the driver or conductor on board, or by contactless domestic bank card on trams and trolleybuses; there is no single rechargeable smart-card system across all modes, and foreign-issued cards do not work in Russia.
transit.hours: Trams and trolleybuses run roughly 06:00-23:00; marshrutka minibuses fill the gaps and some run a little later, but there is no all-night service.
transit.note: Marshrutka shared minibuses are the fastest way around; the tram and trolleybus network covers the central districts and is very cheap.

train: Irkutsk-Passazhirsky station on the Trans-Siberian Railway - trains to Moscow, Vladivostok and Ulan-Ude, plus the scenic Circum-Baikal line
bus: Irkutsk Bus Station (Avtovokzal) - coaches and marshrutkas to Listvyanka, Arshan and regional towns
ferry: Seasonal hydrofoils and boats on the Angara River and to Lake Baikal (Listvyanka, Olkhon Island) in summer

transit.m: Trolleybus / bus / marshrutka to the city center (25-35 min)
Yandex Go / taxi to the center (15-25 min)

tip.r: Not obligatory; rounding up or leaving 5-10% at restaurants for good service is appreciated but not expected.
